criteria.note: autoUpdate.test.ts: 'queries the feed again on the scheduled poll' and 'queries the feed again on the manual Check for updates request'; canStartUpdateCheck table test updated to accept downloaded.
Test 'moves to a newer version through available, downloading and downloaded': goes from downloaded 9.0.0 to 9.1.0. availableVersion and the message name 9.1.0 at each step.

Tests 'keeps the downloaded update ready when the feed has nothing newer' and '...when the feed re-announces the same version': stays downloaded 9.0.0 with 'Version 9.0.0 is ready.'; the banner shows Restart now whenever the phase is downloaded.

Chosen behavior: keep the earlier download whenever it still exists. A failure before a newer version is announced (error event or rejected checkForUpdates) keeps downloaded and Restart now and only logs. Once a newer version is announced, electron-updater 6.8.9 deletes the cached installer (cleanCacheDirForPendingUpdate), so a failed newer download becomes error and the next manual check or poll downloads the newest version again. Tests: 'keeps the downloaded update ready when the re-check itself fails' and 'reports an error and allows a fresh check when a newer download fails'.

Tests 'does not start a check while checking, available or downloading' and 'skips overlapping re-checks while a downloaded update is ready', plus the existing overlap and disabled-update tests. All 17 pass.
autoUpdate tests 17/17, npm run lint and npm run typecheck all pass.

outputs.summary: Check for updates and the 4-hour poll now run in phase `downloaded` (canStartUpdateCheck allows downloaded; checkInFlight guard unchanged). While an update is ready, checking-for-update, update-not-available and a re-announced same version leave the state untouched, so Restart now stays. A newer version moves the state through available, downloading and downloaded for that version. Errors go through a new reportUpdateError: a failure while still `downloaded` (before a newer version is announced) keeps the ready update and only logs; a failed newer download becomes `error`, from which the next check recovers. The auto-update runbook was updated to describe the new behavior.
